Recap:
- Goal: Secure private connectivity from FinPay's VPC to Redwood Private for inference (VPC endpoints + IP allowlist, egress controls, DNS, mTLS where possible).
- Minimum required items for PoC: IP ranges for allowlist, preferred egress model (via NAT vs PrivateLink), DNS resolution for redwood-internal endpoints, and whether mTLS cert management is preferred by you or by Redwood.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Please share the three CIDR blocks you plan to use for outbound allowlist (we'll add as examples in the PoC checklist).
2) Marissa will send the SDK/auth quickstart and the VPC checklist (attached) with specific ports/URLs.
3) Jonas will confirm mTLS options and provide the cert thumbprint flow.
4) We'll target a PoC start on Apr 12 - confirm availability.

I've attached a network diagram and our VPC checklist for your infra team. Happy to hop on a call with your network/security folks this week if useful.

\u0014Lauren

From: Amit Shah <amit@finpay.com>

Subject: Re: VPC endpoints & IP allowlist - next steps

Thanks Lauren - helpful summary. Two quick clarifications from our side:

- CIDRs: We can provide three ephemeral NAT egress ranges from our prod VPC: 10.10.0.0/22, 10.20.0.0/22, 10.30.0.0/22. Will that work? We also have a separate mgmt VPC if you prefer a single IP for control plane traffic.
- Egress: For the PoC we'd prefer to keep traffic inside private network if possible (PrivateLink/Interface Endpoint). NAT egress is acceptable for initial tests but we want to move to endpoints for production.
- mTLS: Security prefers mTLS for control-plane calls; they asked if Redwood can support client cert rotation via our internal CA (we can provide certs) or if Redwood requires Let's Encrypt style termination.

Samantha (CC) is our infra lead and will join network call.

Amit
Senior Product Manager
FinPay

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit@finpay.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC endpoints & IP allowlist - next steps

Hi Amit - looping in details for the infra team. Attached checklist has ports and endpoint DNS names; short answers below:

- CIDRs: Those three /22 ranges are fine for our PoC. If you can provide the mgmt VPC single IP for control plane traffic that simplifies ACLs.
- Private connectivity: We support VPC Interface Endpoints (PrivateLink) for AWS and Private Service Connect on GCP. For PoC we can accept NAT egress but recommend Interface Endpoint for production to avoid egress costs and reduce path complexity.
- DNS: For PrivateLink we publish private hosted zone names (redwood-internal.<region>.rwd) - we'll provide the exact zone names in the drive doc.
- mTLS: We support TLS termination at our edge; for mutual TLS we can accept client certs. For cert rotation we support both options: you can push certs to us via secure upload or integrate with your KMS/HSM and we'll fetch as needed. Jonas will add the exact cert thumbprint verification steps below.

Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-vpc-checklist.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC endpoints & IP allowlist - mTLS and cert flow

Amit - quick technical note on mTLS and IP allowlist flows.

- Client certs: We support uploading PEM-formatted client certs (X.509) to our private control plane. For rotation we prefer that FinPay either (a) push new certs to our secure upload endpoint and notify us, or (b) publish certs to a well-known S3 bucket and notify Redwood to fetch on schedule. Both are supported.
- Thumbprint verification: We'll store the cert thumbprint and reject connections without a matching thumbprint. We can also accept a CRL/OCSP flow if you want certificate revocation checks.
- Ports/Protocols: For Interface Endpoint path we use HTTPS over 443 with SNI redwood-internal.<region>.rwd; if you choose NAT egress the same endpoints are reachable but via public resolvable names - use the allowlist provided.
- Firewall rules: Outbound to our control plane: 3 IPs (listed in checklist) over TCP 443. For data plane (inference traffic) expect ephemeral connections initiated from your VPC to our dedicated pool - we'll provide per-PoC ranges.

I'll draft a short Ops runbook and drop it into the Drive link Lauren shared.

\u0014Jonas
Security/Infra
Redwood Inference
